text:
Priya S: Heads-up: I opened a docs PR with a migration checklist for old tool-call shapes -> our recommended `parse_result` envelope. It's in draft and I'd like quick feedback on the mapping rules.

Ethan L: Nice. Can you paste the decision snippets here so we can eyeball?

Priya S: Sure. Core mappings I'm proposing:

```
old: {"tool_call": {"name":"do_x","arguments":"{\"id\":1}"}}
new: {"parse_result": {"status":"ok","call": {"name":"do_x","arguments": {"id":1}}}}

old: ["a","b"]
new: {"parse_result": {"status":"ok","call": {"name":"list_items","arguments":{"items":["a","b"]}}}}
```

Marta V: I like the conservative approach. A couple notes: 1) show a deterministic transform for string-encoded JSON in `arguments` (parse then attach). 2) warn about lossy heuristics when `arguments` contains natural language.

Samir R: Also recommend adding an RFC-style snippet for teams that can't move to envelopes yet: show a robust regex to extract a top-level object. Example I use in infra: `/(\{[\s\S]*\})/m` and take group 1.

Priya S: Good call. I'll add both: a recommended transform and a lenient-extract fallback with clear warning.

Ethan L: We should split the docs changes into 3 PRs to keep reviews small: 1) canonical examples + migration table, 2) SDK snippet updates (Node/Python), 3) test fixtures + harness.

Priya S: Agree. I'll keep the migration table PR small. Can someone volunteer for the SDK snippets? Node + Go would be ideal.

Marta V: I'll take Go. I'll include an example that uses `json.RawMessage` for safe handling.

Samir R: I'll do Node. I'll also add a tiny unit test showing `lenientExtract` -> `JSON.parse` and the `unparseable` envelope.

RepoBot: New PR created by Priya S: docs#4201 "migration: normalize tool-call shapes to parse_result" (reviewers: Ethan L, Marta V, Samir R).

Ethan L: Quick link fix: docs reference to the function-calling spec still points at the internal RFC. Replace with `https://docs.redwood.ai/function-calling-spec` in all examples.

Priya S: Thanks — updating links now. Also adding a short note in the changelog: "Docs: clarify structured output and introduce migration guidance (examples + SDK snippets)".

Marta V: For the Go snippet, I'll include this pattern:

```
var raw = lenientExtract(respText)
var out struct{ParseResult json.RawMessage `json:"parse_result"`}
if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(raw), &out); err != nil { /* emit unparseable envelope */ }
```

Samir R: For Node I'll add a helper similar to our other SDKs: `extractJson(text)` + try/catch JSON.parse then fallback to `{ parse_result: { status: 'unparseable', raw: text } }`.

Ethan L: Reminder: update the docs cross-links to the SDK repo so the snippets live next to tests. Should reduce drift.

Priya S: Good point. I'll add a `snippets/` pointer in the migration doc that links to `https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs-snippets` where we'll land tests.

RepoBot: docs#4201 set to needs-review (Ethan L, Marta V, Samir R).

Marta V: One editorial nit: use "shape normalization" instead of "auto-parsing" in headings. Less ambiguous.

Priya S: Done. Also adding an explicit section: "When NOT to use lenient-extract" with examples where strict validation is required (PII contexts, signed payloads).

Samir R: I'll prepare the Node snippet PR and include a small test that runs against three captured responses: noisy-preface, string-encoded-arguments, and bare-array.

Ethan L: I'll review once PRs are split. Can we aim to land migration table + link fixes by Wednesday? SDK + tests can follow by Friday.

Priya S: Timeline sounds good. If we hit blocker, we'll add an II-flag and hold the release note mention until SDKs are updated.

RepoBot: PR docs#4201 merged by Priya S (migration table + links).

Priya S: Thanks all. Next steps: Samir + Marta open SDK PRs, Samir attaches test fixtures, Ethan does final docs pass. I'll add a short entry in the release notes once SDK PRs merge.

Ethan L: Thx — ping when Node + Go PRs are ready and I'll do a final read.
